card.name: Linking words before burden-of-disease terms
card.fires_on: Small linking words (of, and, include, to) in public-health text about the toll of disease, where a loss-type word such as lost days, disability or lost time could come next.

modes.label: Burden of illness
modes.description: A linking word after phrases about the share or cost of disease, such as a proportion of disabilities or causes of death.
modes.example: Major depression and other mood disorders account for a substantial proportion<< of>> medical disabilities in the United States.

modes.label: Death and disability lists
modes.description: The word and after leading causes of death, before disability.
modes.example: are the leading causes of death<< and>> disability worldwide and account for 75

modes.label: Costs to people
modes.description: A verb or article introducing what illness costs patients and families.
modes.example: Costs to individuals and their families<< include>> drugs, travel to and treatment at clinics

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words about loss, such as lost, loss and lose, as the next word.
card.plain: It fires on small linking words in sentences about how much disease costs people, where words like lost or loss may come next.
